faqs.q: At the time of independence, India was a signatory to approximately how many treaties?

options.d: More than a million soldiers contributed to the war

faqs.a: More than a million soldiers contributed to the war

faqs.q:

From which year was there an Indian high commissioner in London?
Which of the following expansionist expeditions undertaken by the British after 1878 was opposed by the Indian nationalists?
faqs.e: The Second Afghan War (1878-80) was among the post-1878 expansionist expeditions the nationalists opposed.

faqs.q: Nehru laid the foundations of independent India's foreign policy in his address to the Constituent Assembly on which date?
Panchsheel, or the Five Principles of Peaceful Co-existence, was first formally enunciated on which date?
faqs.e: It was enunciated in the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet region of China and India.

faqs.q: The Agreement embodying Panchsheel concerned trade and intercourse between India and which region?

Consider the following as being among the Five Principles of Peaceful Co-existence:
(I) Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
(II) Mutual non-aggression
(III) Equality and mutual benefit
Which of the above is/are correct?
The joint statement elaborating Panchsheel as a framework for India-China relations was issued in June 1954 during whose visit to India?
As per the historical perspective on Panchsheel, credit for formulating the five principles is attributed to whom?
faqs.e: Zhou first enunciated them as "five principles governing China's relations with foreign countries" while receiving the Indian delegation to the Tibetan trade talks on December 31, 1953.

faqs.q: Who, as a joint secretary in the external affairs ministry, took the initiative to include the five principles at the outset of the draft agreement text in January 1954?
Panchsheel was incorporated into the Ten Principles of International Peace and Cooperation put forward at the Bandung Conference held in which month and year?

Consider the following statements:
(I) A UN resolution on peaceful co-existence incorporating Panchsheel's tenets was presented by India, Yugoslavia and Sweden.
(II) This resolution was unanimously adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 11, 1957.
(III) The Belgrade Conference of Non-Aligned Nations in 1961 accepted Panchsheel as the basic principles of the Non-Aligned Movement.
Which of the above is/are correct?
The term 'non-alignment' got currency in the aftermath of which conference?
The first Non-Aligned Movement summit was held in Belgrade in which year?
faqs.e: It was attended by 36 Mediterranean and Afro-Asian powers.

faqs.q: Which of the following pioneering leaders of the Non-Aligned Movement was the President of Egypt?
What was the original name of Yugoslavia's President Tito, a pioneering leader of the NAM?
How does non-alignment differ from neutrality as India's foreign policy stance?

options.b: Neutrality is passive and confined to wartime, while non-alignment involves positive, constructive opinions applicable in both war and peace
options.c: Non-alignment applies only during war, neutrality applies at all times
options.d: Non-alignment means having no opinion on international issues

faqs.a: Neutrality is passive and confined to wartime, while non-alignment involves positive, constructive opinions applicable in both war and peace

faqs.q: The Preparatory Committee of the first non-aligned conference laid down criteria of non-alignment. Which of the following was one such criterion?

options.a: Compulsory membership of the United Nations
options.b: Consistent support for national freedom movements in other countries
options.d: Alignment with at least one super power

faqs.a: Consistent support for national freedom movements in other countries
